newsitem.title: USA: First Empire Q1 net charge-offs higher.
newsitem.headline: First Empire Q1 net charge-offs higher.

text.p: First Empire State Corp said on Tuesday that for the first quarter of 1997 it had net charge-offs of $7.9 million, compared with $5.1 million for the same period in 1996.
The increase reflected higher charge-offs of consumer loans, the company said.
Assets taken in foreclosure of defaulted loans were $8.7 million at March 31, 1997 and $7.5 million at March 31, 1996, the company said.

The provision for possible credit losses was $11.0 million in the first quarter of 1997, compared with $9.7 million a year ago, First Empire said. The allowance for possible credit losses was $273.6 million or 2.53 percent of total loans at March 31, 1997, compared with $266.9 million or 2.69 percent a year earlier.
Average loans outstanding increased 11 percent to $10.7 billion in the recent quarter, from $9.7 billion in the first quarter of 1996.
